JPM.thesis: Sector relative-strength reading: financials are rolling over, high-yield spreads are widening, and the author sees stress building in bank balance sheets; he flags JPM specifically as the lead name for multiple compression.

GS.thesis: Chart pattern (bear flag) plus the broader thesis that banks are the next group to crack as credit spreads widen and corporate debt issuance crowds the market.

RKLB.thesis: Chart-based watchlist call; no further reasoning given.

Years of acquisitions assembled a full spacecraft stack that forms a moat, so Rocket Lab can monetize a mission whether it wins the prime contract or supplies components. The backlog shows demand is already there.
A top-three holding; the author sees Rocket Lab as a generational space company and views panic selling as transfer to long-term holders.

META.thesis: Meta's installed base lets a free product scale instantly. Muse adds connectors, payments (Shopify, PayPal, Meta Pay), glasses and dedicated hardware, and the transaction-fee model expands the TAM. The author built conviction before the narrative turned.
Author's belief in Meta's long-term value; no fundamental reasoning given.
META was criticised for AI-leader-level spending without an AI product to show for it; Muse supplies that product and becomes the earnings catalyst.
One of the author's top three portfolio positions; the author asserts the market underappreciates it, without laying out fundamentals in these posts.

ON.thesis: The 800V transition multiplies power-semiconductor content per AI rack, and all that compute still has to be powered.

P.thesis: Once AI runs everywhere, the constraint becomes how efficiently data is fed, stored and retrieved, and Everpure's guidance is starting to reflect that.

VRT.thesis: If GPU and TPU compute keeps scaling, the bottleneck moves to powering and cooling the racks, and this theme is still early.

IREN.thesis: Energized sites are the scarcest input, and lenders price that asset more cheaply than GPU-heavy balance sheets, which gives IREN the lowest cost of capital among the neoclouds.
Chart breakout, picked over CIFR and NBIS as the name about to break out.

NBIS.thesis: Customer-prepaid capex keeps the funding model cleaner than CoreWeave's, and repeated price hikes plus spot pricing show demand exceeding supply.
Chart breakout in AI infrastructure; the author has long called for a much higher target.

NVDA.thesis: Nvidia's growth and margins in the largest infrastructure buildout since the internet do not justify its valuation discount, and physical AI has barely reached its numbers.
Best business but too large to 'make you rich'; take profits and rotate into higher-growth names, while still 'continue to buy'.
A bearish rising wedge in Wave 5 and failure at resistance signal buyers are slowing and rotating to better opportunities; not a verdict on company quality.

MU.thesis: AI servers drive most incremental DRAM demand while supply bit growth lags, so HBM and NAND pricing stays strong.
Memory is the dominant cycle of 2026+; companies with the best memory exposure improve margins and the industry pivot toward memory is happening rapidly.
HBM/DRAM leadership in AI memory, analyst Strong Buy ratings, relayed AI-chatbot rankings.
Memory led the last major AI move and is breaking out again; bought at major daily demand when others were scared of AI and memory names.

Inference and agentic AI multiply memory demand while fab output is finite; HBM consumes several times the wafer capacity per bit, supply is sold out to LTA holders, and capex dollars are shifting toward memory at very high margins.

SKHY.thesis: Server DRAM demand from AI and constrained supply push HBM pricing higher for the leading HBM suppliers.
One of three memory makers controlling finite fab output while HBM demand from GPUs, TPUs and custom ASICs keeps doubling; 8-high HBM4 carries better yields and pricing.

AMD.thesis: Consumer agents such as Muse still need CPUs for tool calls, orchestration and data movement alongside GPUs, which gives AMD another way to monetize the agentic buildout.
AI compute share gains, analyst Strong Buy ratings, CEO Lisa Su's insider purchase, and smaller market cap giving more upside than NVIDIA.
Parabolic moves in Wave 5 indicate the top is approaching.
Agentic AI drives CPU demand, not just memory; chart showed a BLUE signal off Bollinger basis support confirmed by GREEN.

SOFI.thesis: The loan platform business and fee businesses monetize volume without holding the credit, and stablecoin settlement on the card program shows the platform expanding.

HOOD.thesis: Net interest revenue is a large share of revenue and benefits from elevated rates, and zero-coupon convertible debt gives Robinhood cheap capital while rates stay high.
Called underrated; no further reasoning given.

APP.thesis: The market is not pricing continued AXON improvement, but gaming is maturing.

QCOM.thesis: New AI data-center interconnect and edge-AI moves show Qualcomm working deeper into the AI stack.

ALAB.thesis: CXL is the largest byproduct of the memory industry, and Astera Labs is the CXL play; recent breakout from a long sideways range confirms emerging strength.

SNDK.thesis: Grouped with Micron as a core memory-cycle name; the author credits himself with calling the CPU and memory run that lifted Sandisk.
High-beta memory/storage cycle exposure to AI demand, analyst Strong Buy ratings, and Seeking Alpha Alpha Picks ownership.
Part of the memory group that led the last AI move and is breaking out again; bought at major daily demand.
Agentic AI context data cannot all live in HBM and overflows to NAND, and heavy AI read/write cycles force hyperscalers to overprovision or replace NAND more often; TrendForce rates NAND tight.

RARE.thesis: A rare way to get gene-therapy exposure through a company with an approved, commercialized gene therapy rather than a clinical-stage bet; not a typical retail name.

WGS.thesis: A completed trade the author has exited and moved on from.

MRVL.thesis: AI networking, optics and custom silicon exposure, endorsement by NVIDIA's Jensen Huang, perceived underpricing and a possible short squeeze.

CRDO.thesis: Exploding AI data-center connectivity demand, smaller market cap, Point72 and Seeking Alpha ownership.

SPCX.thesis: Space economy exposure; preferred over Tesla, partly echoing AI-chatbot comparisons.

AKAM.thesis: The relevance of Akamai's technology and infrastructure suite is increasing. He first published this thesis in August, re-entered the day before the Anthropic deal was announced, and treats the deal as confirmation.

ORCL.thesis: A large fixed-rate debt stack repriced at today's curve raises coupons materially, while elevated capex and deeply negative FCF increase financing needs, leaving the curve wide of BBB and creating a feedback loop of weaker FCF, more borrowing and weaker coverage.

ARM.thesis: Grouped with the AI/memory names bought at major daily demand; named a semiconductor leader under the SMH/EUV ETFs.

INTC.thesis: Semis that led the last AI move are breaking out again; he traded it with his 8/21 cross break-and-retest setup.

BABA.thesis: Insiders bought near current levels, revenue has compounded while the share price has gone nowhere, free cash flow is being reinvested, a global AI data-center push, and price action echoing Trump's first term which the author views as bullish for China.

ASTS.thesis: Best-in-market chart, moat and management, and global uninterrupted connectivity is a prerequisite for AI, space and humanoids, a market the author expects Starlink and ASTS to dominate.

SE.thesis: Listed among good companies that were not buys at high prices but are now at value prices; otherwise signalled with 'IYKYK' teasers.

ZETA.thesis: Consistent revenue beats and management quality; the author draws the Palantir analogy.

HIMS.thesis: The author doubled the position under the 200 WMA and argues the market is starting to see what he sees.

ADUR.thesis: Positive plastic-recycling (hydrocarbon yield) campaign results and a management team the author praises.

COIN.thesis: Crypto leaders ETH and BTC moving; Coinbase reclaimed its 200 WMA after being flagged below it.

DELL.thesis: Dell hit its extended Wave 5 Fibonacci target; parabolic Wave 5 moves mark tops and smart money exits into retail.

NVO.thesis: Valuation discipline: good company, wrong price.

TSM.thesis: TSMC is becoming the dominant CPU maker and advanced packaging is the only way to achieve high bandwidth by bringing chips closer together.
